I. Forge Legendary Games: Start from the Genes In Star of Games, creating games is no longer just about combining genres. In the vast world of Star of Games, you are not alone. Encounter Legends, as Rivals or Allies : Well-known companies will be your inspirations, your competitors, and potential partners. Compete with them for Game of the Year, collaborate to gain tech licenses, or even participate in developing their legendary sequels. R ecruit Masters, Nurture New Talent : As you rise to prominence, legendary producers might appear, offering guidance, tasks, or even a chance to recruit them! The personal dramas of employees, competitors' business secrets, and the birth of legends are all dynamically generated by your choices. Ultimate Freedom of Exploration : From game concepts to corporate strategy, talent management to business alliances—there is no single formula for success. Every path can lead to your own version of Rome. The main inspirations come from Neo Scavenger, Gates of Hell, RimWorld. The story background is inspired by pivotal conflicts in modern history. You will take on the role of the only surviving officer in the company after an enemy airstrike, taking up the responsibility in a crisis, gathering the remnants, and leading the troops through battle after battle to break through the dilemma, gradually growing into an elite force. Gameplay Design It’s more important to play a bad hand well than to be dealt a good one. Through the high-altitude drone combat command platform, you cannot participate in combat personally, but you can observe the real-time situation on the battlefield and quickly update your combat deployments via the drone’s camera. However, there is still a time gap and human factors in the issuing and execution of orders. Sometimes, you must anticipate in advance or radically shift your approach. But plans never keep up with changes — perhaps you should be prepared for your operations to be disrupted. Frontline Logistics: Isarian Warfare is dedicated to expressing aspects rarely touched upon by other war games: Detailed classification of logistics work. Machine gun ammo belts must be assembled from loose rounds in the ammo workshop before they can be used by gunners; ingredients are cooked into hot meals in the field kitchen; the severely wounded undergo emergency surgery before being transported to the rear for treatment; fallen comrades are recovered, prepared, and sent back. When there are no suitable replacement parts, or when you have two tanks each with different damages, “working” is the only requirement — if it can be fixed, it must not be scrapped! In addition, you can also modify your armament to add new functions to suit different battlefield environments. Soldiers who obey orders but retain individuality. Your soldiers execute combat orders strictly, but may also pick up loot amid the hail of bullets. Besides ammunition, their backpacks may also carry “junk” they can’t bear to discard — if deployed near a river, they might even bring back a big fish for the mess hall in the evening. Balanced nutrition, properly rationed. Frontline Logistics: Isarian Warfare strongly encourages players to enhance the frontline living conditions of their troops in every possible way — and rations are a key part of that. In the game, you can recreate real-world rationing systems used across various theaters of war: rear-echelon logistics personnel receive standard provisions, while frontline combat units are kept well-fed and ready for action. evidence.chinaDemandEvidence: You're a security officer deep within Area 51. Scan the staff, verify clearances, and decide who can enter the elevator and who absolutely mustn't leave. The deeper you go, the less certain you are that anyone standing before you is still human. A "SIMPLE" JOB Security 51 is an atmospheric horror security guard simulator inspired by Papers, Please, and SCP paranoia. You're on duty in the underground bunker of Area 51, where the most dangerous part begins at the elevator: the shaft descends for miles down to unknown levels. Whether it's laboratories, anomalies, inhumane experiments, or something alien—you're not supposed to know. Your task is simple: let in those who have access and stop those who don't... even if everything looks "right" on the surface. SECURE, CONTAIN, PROTECT Everyone who passes through your checkpoint carries papers, passes, or verbal orders. Your job is to check names, positions, clearance levels, and time, ensuring the number of people entering and leaving matches, and pay attention to any oddities. These could be incorrect answers, behavior that deviates from protocol, slurred speech, or even documents that seem too perfect. As time passes you'll catch yourself thinking that something's wrong more and more, and the only thing to rely on will be the protocols. But even they can be wrong. TOTAL CONTROL With experience, you'll gain increasingly more accurate methods of identity verification, such as fingerprint verification or blood testing. Did that janitor simply open the wrong door, or are they a spy for an enemy government? Or are they not even human? When in doubt, quarantine the suspect. Sometimes you'll make mistakes and lock up an ordinary employee, and sometimes you'll find a titanium cell ripped open from the inside. Some decisions will have immediate consequences, others only after several shifts. CONTAIN THE THREAT The consequences of every mistake go far beyond issues in the workplace. Let the wrong person out, and the infection will ravage the city. Isolate suspicious employees, investigate anomalies, and launch new operations to contain the threat before it's too late. Remember, it's not just about who you let in, but who or what you let out into the world. Your job is to build a structure that works: find the right coach, surround him with the right team, and give him the players he needs to compete. If you do it well, results will come. If not, the consequences will be yours. A club is a company, and you run it FD 27 reproduces the real structure of a professional football club. You don't just manage a squad of players, you manage a complete organization with four departments that need to work as one gear: Sporting Direction, Medical Department, Marketing, and Financial Department. Each department is made up of staff members with their own attributes, performance, and salary. You decide who to hire, who to fire, and how much you are willing to pay for the talent you need. The sporting director will be your right-hand in the transfer market. The head of medical will determine how your players recover from injuries and how long they take to return to the pitch. The marketing department will influence the club's ability to attract sponsors and generate revenue. The financial area will keep the accounts in order, or not, depending on who you put in charge. Every hiring has a direct impact on the overall performance of the club. A good sporting director will bring you better signing options. A mediocre medical team will mean your players spend more time in the infirmary than on the pitch. Everything is connected, and everything depends on you. It's not just about having the best eleven. It's about having the best structure. The clubs that win leagues don't do it only because of their players, they do it because behind them there is a solid organization that allows everything to function. That is your job. That is FD 27. Matches are won in the office When match day arrives, you have already done your work. You signed the players, hired the coach, and gave him the tools to compete. Now it's your turn to sit down and see if your decisions were the right ones. FD 27's simulation engine reproduces every match minute by minute, with a system that takes into account dozens of variables: the individual quality of each player, their form, their accumulated fatigue level, their morale, the injuries they carry, and the tactical capacity of the coaching staff. You won't see a static match or a simple final result. You will see how your team wears down physically over the ninety minutes, how a player with low morale performs below his level, how an unexpected injury in the 30th minute forces the coach to restructure the team. The substitution system respects the current three-window rules, and the coaching staff's artificial intelligence makes decisions based on the context of the match: if it's losing, if a player is exhausted, if it needs to protect a result. Every match is a direct consequence of what you have built. If you invested in a good medical team, your players will arrive fresher. If you signed a coach with good tactical reading, the substitutions will be smarter. If you cut corners on the squad, you'll pay for it when the season gets tough and injuries pile up. In FD 27, matches are not won with instructions from the sideline, they are won with the decisions you made weeks, months, and seasons before. Finances, signings, and the art of building without sinking Money is everything and at the same time isn't enough. You can have the biggest budget in the league, but if you manage it poorly, you'll end up in a spiral of debt that will drag the club down for years. FD 27 puts you at the helm of a club's real finances: revenue from television, ticketing, merchandising, and sponsorships against expenses in salaries, signings, infrastructure, and personnel. The transfer market is where great projects are forged and where poorly planned ones die. Every player has a transfer cost and a salary that will impact your accounts throughout the duration of their contract. Signing the star everyone wants can give you an immediate competitive leap, but it can also compromise your ability to strengthen other positions. Would you rather have a star and an unbalanced team, or a well-rounded squad that competes on all fronts? That tension between ambition and sustainability is the heart of the game. Sponsors are another key piece of your financial strategy. As your club grows in reputation and results, new brands will want to associate with you. Each sponsorship contract has its conditions, its duration, and its economic impact. Negotiating well can give you the margin you need to sign that midfielder you're missing. Negotiating poorly can leave you tied to a deal that doesn't reflect the real value of your club. Financial management is not a complement to the game, it is the game. Leagues, players, challenges FD 27 in its version 0.1 includes the leagues of Spain and England. Thousands of players with detailed and position-specific attributes form the squads of the clubs you'll find in the game. A full-back who joins the attack is not the same as one who prioritizes defensive cover, and that is reflected in every player profile. Each league has its own dynamic. The AI teams compete with each other under the same rules as you: their players get tired, get injured, lose form, and experience good and bad streaks. There are no hidden advantages or shortcuts for the machine. The simulation is fair and symmetrical, which means your victories will be deserved and your defeats will have a real explanation. The game is designed to grow. The Spanish and English leagues are the starting point, but the plan includes incorporating new national competitions, leagues from other European countries, and continental competitions that will expand the scope and depth of every game. Each new league won't just be one more setting, it will be a new market with different players, rules, and challenges that will enrich your experience as a director. A game under construction, with your voice as a guide FD 27 is in active development and will arrive on Steam in Early Access. This means you are entering a living project that grows with every update. The foundations are already built: the simulation engine, the staff system, the finances, the sponsorships, and the management interface are already working. But what's coming is even more ambitious. On the horizon are European competitions, a youth academy system to develop talent from the age of 12, the possibility of selling club shares to obtain financing, league assemblies, and random events. Each update will bring new features that will expand what you can do as a director. This is not a game made by a large studio with a million-dollar budget. It is an indie project made with passion for football and management games, inspired by those classics that hooked you for hours. Your feedback matters. Your suggestions will shape development. evidence.chinaDemandEvidence: Wardwell is a Chinese folklore-inspired idle management game. As the ancient well calls, waters surge beneath the earth and omens warn of the Drought Demon’s return. Restore the shrine, manage incense, welcome worshippers, and uncover the mystery buried below. The ancient well is calling, and the waters beneath the earth are beginning to surge. Cracked soil and unnatural moisture spread through the village at the same time. Every omen points toward an old and forbidden legend: the Drought Demon is about to awaken. To keep the disturbances from spreading, you must take charge of the abandoned ritual grounds surrounding the well. Clear away burnt incense, rebuild the shrine, welcome returning worshippers, and gather the resources needed to investigate each new call from below. Wardwell is an idle management game inspired by Chinese folklore and supernatural tales. There is no high-pressure real-time combat. Instead, you will manage the shrine, plan your resources, and unlock new paths of progression as ominous events unfold around the ancient well. The Well Calls, and the Omens Draw Near The ancient well will not remain silent. As time passes, supernatural events progress through charging, warning, manifestation, and resolution stages. Water surging beneath the earth, gathering spiritual energy, and signs of the Drought Demon’s return gradually appear through environmental changes and event sequences. Wandering spirits, jiangshi, and water ghosts may also emerge alongside the well’s disturbances, leaving behind strange tales and unusual materials. Every event is both an omen and an opportunity to learn more about the well, unlock new developments, and reveal what lies ahead. These events are not conventional real-time battles. Your accumulated resources, unlocked content, and the development of the shrine determine how prepared you are for the intensifying disturbances. Build an Economy from Burnt Incense Burnt incense continuously accumulates around the shrine. At first, every piece must be cleared by hand. As your operation develops, you can unlock brooms for batch clearing and Clean Wind Talismans that automatically remove burnt incense over time. Restoring the small incense burner increases the amount produced during each cycle while also providing a steady source of incense income. Clear the remains, gather incense, invest in upgrades, and unlock new ways to make the cycle increasingly efficient. Restore the Abandoned Shrine Spend incense to restore the small incense burner, offering stone, wish rack, and merit box. Each facility has its own method of production and can affect both worshipper offerings and the shrine’s overall income. What begins as slow manual collection can gradually develop into a growing system of batch processing, continuous production, and automation. How you invest your limited incense determines whether you pursue immediate gains or save resources for future events and progression nodes. Welcome Visiting Worshippers Worshippers travel along the village roads to reach the shrine, stopping at different facilities before making their offerings. Each visitor has their own fortune, which can influence both the journey and the result of the offering. Improve facilities and traditions to increase the value of their visits. Observe the flow of worshippers and plan your development so that their offerings become a stable part of the shrine’s economy. Their arrival is also a sign that the villagers still believe the restored shrine can withstand the omens gathering around the well.
